record.paper_title: Padua points and “fake” nodes for polynomial approximation: old, new and open problems
record.original_question: For fake-node and mapped-basis polynomial approximation methods, what rigorous error analysis and tight Lebesgue-constant bounds can be proved, especially for stable variants used to address Runge and Gibbs phenomena?

evidence.quote: Error analysis and tight Lebesgue constant bounds should be investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact set and let $X = \{x_1,\dots,x_N\} \subset \Omega$ be a set of interpolation nodes. Given a continuous injective map $S : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$, define the "fake nodes" as $S(X) = \{S(x_1),\dots,S(x_N)\}$. For a function $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, the mapped-basis (fake-node) polynomial interpolant of degree at most $n$ is defined by
\[
P_n^S[f](x) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^N f(x_i)\, \ell_i^S(x), \qquad \ell_i^S(x) = L_i\big(S(x)\big),
\]
where $\{L_i\}$ is the Lagrange basis of polynomial interpolation on the nodes $S(X)$ in the variable $y = S(x)$. The associated Lebesgue function and Lebesgue constant are
\[
\lambda_n^S(x) = \sum_{i=1}^N |\ell_i^S(x)|, \qquad \Lambda_n^S(\Omega) = \max_{x \in \Omega} \lambda_n^S(x).
\]
Particular instances of interest include the $S$-Runge map (designed to mitigate the Runge phenomenon by mapping equispaced nodes to Chebyshev-like nodes) and the $S$-Gibbs map together with the GRASPA discontinuous-mapping variant (designed to mitigate the Gibbs phenomenon at jump discontinuities).

Problem. For the fake-node / mapped-basis polynomial interpolation scheme above:

(a) Establish rigorous a priori error bounds for $\|f - P_n^S[f]\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$ in terms of smoothness properties of $f$, the geometry of $S(X)$, and analytic properties of the map $S$, valid in both the univariate and multivariate settings.

(b) Prove sharp (matching upper and lower) asymptotic bounds on the Lebesgue constant $\Lambda_n^S(\Omega)$ for the $S$-Runge map, the $S$-Gibbs map, and the GRASPA discontinuous mapped-basis variant, including stability estimates that quantify the conditioning of the scheme as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: several papers establish error analyses and Lebesgue-constant bounds for specific fake-node / mapped-basis schemes (S-Runge, S-Gibbs, GRASPA), inheriting bounds from the mapped node set (e.g., Chebyshev-Lobatto). However, fully general tight Lebesgue-constant bounds and sharp multivariate error analyses for all stable variants remain incomplete, so the broader program is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial interpolation via mapped bases without resampling
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the fake-nodes / mapped-basis approach and provides Lebesgue-constant analysis inherited from mapped nodes.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational Lebesgue-constant analysis for the mapped-basis fake-nodes method has been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Stable discontinuous mapped bases: the GRASPA method
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes the Gibbs-Runge-Avoiding Stable Polynomial Approximation method to mitigate both phenomena and analyzes its stability.
status_evidence.claim: Stable variants addressing Runge and Gibbs phenomena have been developed with partial error/stability analysis.

status_evidence.title: Multivariate approximation at fake nodes
status_evidence.snippet: Extends fake-node analysis to multivariate polynomial approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Multivariate extensions and corresponding error analyses are available, indicating ongoing partial progress.
